checks.title: Compiles against the real Trigger.dev SDK types
checks.why: The submission type-checks against the real SDK, so the primitives are being called with valid shapes.

checks.title: No deprecated Trigger.dev SDK symbols
checks.expected: no @trigger.dev symbols marked @deprecated by the installed SDK
checks.why: Nothing the installed Trigger.dev SDK marks as deprecated is used.

checks.title: No v3-era Trigger.dev APIs
checks.why: The submission uses APIs from Trigger.dev v2/v3 that no longer exist in v4.

evidence.snippet: @trigger.dev/sdk/v3 import path: import { logger, task } from "@trigger.dev/sdk/v3";

checks.title: Tasks are exported so the platform can register them
checks.why: All tasks are exported, which is what makes them discoverable by the worker.

checks.title: Tasks are not invoked by calling run() directly
checks.expected: tasks invoked through trigger/batchTrigger, never task.run()
checks.why: No task body is called directly, so invocations go through the platform.

checks.title: Per-item work runs as its own task
checks.expected: a task per unit of work, dispatched by an orchestrator
checks.why: Per-item work is dispatched to its own task, so each item becomes a run the platform can schedule, retry and observe independently.

checks.title: No second queue or scheduler beside the platform
checks.why: The task does not ask for work to be queued or scheduled.

checks.title: Fan-out uses a batch trigger
checks.why: The task does not require items to be dispatched together.

checks.title: Concurrency limited by a Trigger.dev queue
checks.why: The task does not state a concurrency requirement.

checks.title: Retries handled by the platform retry engine
checks.why: The task does not require recovery from transient failures.

checks.title: Orchestrator waits for every child to finish
checks.why: The orchestrator suspends at a waitpoint until every child run is terminal, which also releases its concurrency slot while it waits.

checks.title: Per-item success and failure read from the run results
checks.expected: waits for the runs and branches on each run's ok flag
checks.why: The orchestrator waits for the child runs and branches on each run's ok flag, so a failed item is reported as failed instead of silently dropped.

checks.title: One failing item does not abort the others
checks.expected: branch on each run's ok flag
checks.actual: reads the ok flag on each run result
checks.why: Each run's outcome is inspected individually, so a failed item is recorded as failed while the rest continue.

checks.title: Concurrent runs do not share in-process state
checks.expected: no task body writing to module-scope state
checks.actual: state is confined to run payloads and metadata
checks.why: No task writes to module-scope state, so two runs of the same workflow cannot read or overwrite each other's data.

checks.title: Waiting checkpoints instead of blocking the process
checks.why: The task does not require durability across interruption.

checks.title: Progress is published through the platform
checks.why: The task does not require observable progress.

checks.title: Cancellation is handled
checks.expected: an onCancel hook or the run's abort signal
checks.why: Nothing handles cancellation. Without an onCancel hook or the run's abort signal, cancelling the parent leaves child work running and any external calls in flight.

checks.title: Waits for an external party without polling
checks.why: The task never waits on anything outside the workflow.

checks.title: Waiting on an outside party has a deadline
checks.why: The task does not wait on anything outside the workflow.

checks.title: Partial output is streamed as it is produced
checks.why: The task does not require incremental output.

checks.title: Memory-hungry work is provisioned and recovers
checks.why: The task has no memory-bound work.

checks.title: Schedules are registered per tenant at runtime
checks.why: The task does not require per-tenant schedules.

checks.title: Higher-priority work is served first
checks.why: The task does not rank classes of work.

checks.title: One tenant's volume does not delay another's
checks.why: The task is not multi-tenant.

checks.title: Replaying the parent does not duplicate work
checks.why: The task does not require replay safety.

checks.title: Fan-out is split to fit the batch size cap
checks.why: The task fans out an unstated number of items, which fits in a single batch of 1000.

checks.title: Large content is passed by reference, not in the payload
checks.expected: a key or id in the payload, with the child fetching the content
checks.actual: payloads carry identifiers rather than content
checks.why: Payloads carry references rather than content, so they stay small regardless of how large the underlying items are and never approach the 3MB trigger cap.

checks.title: Progress reporting stays inside the metadata size cap
checks.why: The task does not require progress to accumulate per item.

checks.title: Aggregated results stay inside the output size cap
checks.expected: the parent returns a summary, not every child's output
checks.actual: child outputs are reduced before being returned
checks.why: The parent reduces the child results to the fields it needs, so its return value stays a summary and cannot grow past the 10MB output cap as items are added.

checks.title: Idempotency keys are scoped to survive a replay
checks.why: The task does not require replay safety.
